title: C# Multiple Choice Questions - Generics
description: This section of our 1000+ C# MCQs focuses on generics in C# Programming Language.

questions.question: What is meant by the term 'generics' in C#?
questions.explanation: Generics allow you to define classes, structures, interfaces, and methods with placeholders (parameters) for the data types they store or manipulate.

questions.question: Are generics in C# implemented in the same way as generics in Java or templates in C++?

options.text: No, there are fundamental differences in implementation
Yes, but only for value types

questions.explanation: C# generics are unique. Unlike Java (which uses erasure) or C++ (which uses template expansion), C# generics are integrated into the CLI runtime and preserve type information at execution (reification).

questions.question: What are the primary advantages of using generics?

options.text: Code reusability with different data types

questions.explanation: Generics provide a way to reuse code efficiently while maintaining strict type checking and avoiding the performance overhead of moving between value and reference types.

questions.question: In C#, what is a construct like 'Gen<T>' (with an unspecified type parameter) called?
questions.explanation: A generic type where at least one type argument is a type parameter (like T) is called an open constructed type.

questions.question: Which of these classes is a member of the System.Collections.Generic namespace?
questions.explanation: Stack<T> is a generic collection. ArrayList and Hashtable are non-generic collections found in the System.Collections namespace.

questions.question: What is the correct syntax for a generic method that takes a type parameter T?
questions.explanation: A generic method must specify the type parameter in angle brackets '<T>' immediately after the method name.

questions.question: Which conventional letter is most commonly used as a placeholder for a generic type argument?
questions.explanation: By convention, 'T' (representing Type) is used. For dictionaries, 'K' (Key) and 'V' (Value) are also common.
